newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Grain monopoly sets premium - Australia's NSWGB.
newsitem.headline: Grain monopoly sets premium - Australia's NSWGB.

text.p: The single desk monopoly sales system by Australia's New South Wales Grains Board (NSWGB) produced premiums of A$7.00-A$12.00 a tonne on malting barley export prices, the board said in its 1995/96 annual report.

This was found in a study in the latest year in the states of Western Australia, South Australia, Victoria and New South Wales (NSW) by the Meyers Strategy Group, Athol Roberts, NSWGB chairman, said in the annual report.
Workshops with NSW farmers also showed that 93 percent wished to retain the current basic NSWGB structure, he said.
NSWGB, a state government statutory body, will be subject to a review by the state government under Australia's national competition policy in 1997.
Roberts said in the annual report that a 1996 state government review of rice marketing legislation similar to the NSW Grain Marketing Act produced a decision for no change until at least year 2004.
In a year of "unrivalled achievement", NSWGB grain accumulation and sales recovered to 1.3 million tonnes and A$325 million from drought-affected 485,000 tonnes and A$100 million in 1994/95, he said.
NSWGB recorded an operating profit before abnormals of A$7.72 million against A$1.33 million the year before, the report shows.
